newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian presidency expected to meet next week.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian presidency expected to meet next week.

text.p: Bosnia's crisis-hit three-man presidency, which has yet to function properly since general elections last month, will meet in Sarajevo next week, Bosnian officials said on Wednesday.

At the same time, the body supervising post-war elections in Bosnia is expected to decide on Thursday whether or not politically sensitive local elections can go ahead as planned next month, Western officials said.
The rotating presidency, comprising Moslem leader Alija Izetbegovic, Croat member Kresimir Zubak and Bosnian Serb Momcilo Krajisnik, met initially after the September 14 general elections.

But it has been unable to take up its work because Krajisnik has refused to sign the required oath of loyalty to a unified Bosnia, something that would negate the Serbs' desire for separate statehood.
Bosnian Foreign Minister Jadranko Prljic said: "According to the latest information, the next meeting of the presidency will be next week. Some kind of approval on that point was received today."
He was speaking at a news conference for visiting Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos.
Pangalos said he had been told by Izetbegovic that the Moslem leader and Krajisnik had confirmed the presidency meeting in a telephone call.
"So we bring you great news," Pangalos told reporters. "It's a great pleasure for everyone in the international community, I think."
Neither Pangalos nor Prljic said exactly where the presidency meeting would be held -- a major sticking point, according to the Serbs.
Bosnian officials said the presidency meeting would focus on government business including the formation of joint institutions.
After the September elections which elected the presidency and parliament, local elections are due on November 23 and 24.

The body supervising the polls, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), has indicated that the local elections may have to be cancelled if agreement cannot be reached on holding them on schedule.

The Bosnian Serbs have threatened to boycott the elections and Western officials say the Bosnian ruling party, the SDA, also has misgivings about the possibility of losing control of some municipalities.

The Provisional Election Commission, an OSCE body, is scheduled to meet in Sarajevo on Thursday and a decision should be reached on whether or not to go ahead with the local elections, Western officials said.
The head of the OSCE mission in Bosnia, Robert Frowick of the United States, has held intense discussions with all sides over the past few days in an attempt to salvage the elections.

Frowick travelled to the town of Banja Luka on Wednesday to meet Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic, a hardline nationalist who has threatened to pull the Serbs out of local polls under OSCE supervision.
